subject: Budget range validation - Voyager Payments
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@voyagerpayments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-02-10T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Budget range validation - Voyager Payments

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and a few follow-ups from our discovery:

- Estimated call/usage profile you shared: ~1.2M API calls/month initially, ~350 tokens per call average (mixed user prompts + system tokens).
- That maps to roughly 420M tokens/month today (1.2M * 350). You mentioned 20% q/q growth expected over first 6 months.
- Procurement thresholds: you indicated internal PO/Proc review kicks in for commitments >$25k/month and VP approval for >$75k/month (please confirm).

Action items I promised:
1) Share a short pricing estimate across three scenarios (PoC, Launch, Scale). Attached is a preliminary PDF (redwood-pricing-estimate.pdf) and a mutual action plan (mutual-action-plan.xlsx).
2) Quick check on target unit economics — you mentioned target TCO of roughly $X per 1M tokens for production usage; can you confirm a target $/1M tokens we should aim for in negotiations?
3) Clarify procurement cadence and required docs (PO lead time, vendor questionnaire, SOC2).

High-level guidance from our side: on hosted API, typical list-level unit economics are in the $900–1200 / 1M tokens range for low-volume usage; with committed reserved capacity we can get to the $300–600 / 1M tokens band depending on volume and term. I put three example bands in the attached estimate.

If the procurement threshold you mentioned is firm (PO at >$25k/month), it helps us prioritize whether to propose a reserved Dedicated plan vs. hosted.

Next steps: could you confirm the target $/1M tokens (or a target monthly spend band) and procurement rules? Happy to set up a short sync with procurement if that's easier.

Thanks —
Dylan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@voyagerpayments.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-02-11T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Budget range validation - Voyager Payments

Thanks Dylan — good recap and thanks for the docs. A few clarifications from our side:

- Volume: the 1.2M calls/month is our conservative estimate for Q1 post-PoC. We expect average token usage to be closer to 300–375 tokens/call depending on the use case mix (customer messages are long; fraud checks are shorter). So 360 tokens/call is a reasonable working number.
- Growth: if the PoC is successful, we have a probationary launch plan that could push us to ~5–10M calls/month within 6–9 months (so tokens scale accordingly).
- Procurement thresholds (confirmed):
  * <$10k/month: Card/standard procurement — no PO required.
  * $10k–$25k/month: Finance notification and standard vendor setup; PO optional.
  * >$25k/month: PO required and procurement review.
  * >$75k/month: VP approval + security/compliance director sign-off.

Target unit economics: our engineering/product stakeholders are targeting ~ $600 / 1M tokens as a target for production (that keeps our per-transaction cost under our margin targets). If you can get closer to $500 / 1M at scale, that would be very compelling.

Attachments: I attached our internal procurement checklist (procurement-checklist.pdf) — happy to share it if it helps align the MAP.

Happy to sync Marissa in and schedule a quick 20-minute procurement intro.

Best,
Samantha Lee
Head of Platform Integrations | Voyager Payments
samantha.lee@voyagerpayments.com | +1 (212) 555-4477

Appreciate the details, Samantha — that's super helpful. Based on the clarified numbers (1.2M calls -> ~432M tokens/month at 360 tokens/call) and your target $600 / 1M tokens, I sketched three pragmatic scenarios in the attached pricing PDF:

- PoC (3 months): 5–10M tokens/month -> estimated hosted price band $4k–$9k/month (list-tier pricing applied).
- Launch: 50M tokens/month -> reserve-eligible pricing; with a 12‑month commit we can target ~$450 / 1M tokens (~$22.5k/month).
- Scale: 200M+ tokens/month -> Dedicated/reserved pricing; with higher commit and quantization/throughput optimizations we can target ~$300–350 / 1M tokens (~$60k/month for 200M tokens at $300/1M).

Notes on unit economics and options:
- Hosted API (no commit) keeps start-up friction low but list-level unit costs are higher.
- Dedicated/Reserved reduces unit cost materially — we typically require a minimum commit/term for the deepest discounts.
- For procurement: if PO required at >$25k/month, Launch and Scale bands will likely trigger procurement review. We recommend planning the MAP and necessary paperwork early so legal/procurement have time to complete vendor setup.

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll update the MAP with the three scenarios and mark which ones will trigger PO/VP approvals.
2) Marissa (cc'd) can join a brief procurement intro call next week (15–20 min) to walk procurement through the MAP and vendor documents (SOC2, SLA, SSO/KMS).
3) If you want formal pricing/quote for procurement, I can follow up with a one-page quotation and a simple SOW.

If the $600 / 1M target is the internal goal, our recommendation is to aim for the Launch band (50M tokens/mo commit) — it's the sweet spot where you get meaningful unit cost reduction without immediate heavy infra commitments.

Thanks —
Dylan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Dylan / Samantha — looping in procurement formally. A couple of items from our side: 

- Procurement asks: please provide a formal quotation (line-item by token band), SOC2 Type II report (or attestation), W9, and a standard Master Services Agreement (MSA) or SOW.
- Our internal thresholds (to confirm with Finance): single-vendor spend >$100k/year requires three bids; for >$25k/month we will need a PO and procurement review (as Samantha noted).
- Timing: procurement lead time is typically 2–3 weeks once we have a quote + SOC2 + W9.

Can you send the formal quote + link to SOC2? We can then put an internal timeline together and decide whether to run an RFP or proceed direct based on your reference and pricing.

Thanks,
Tom Hernandez
Senior Procurement Manager | Voyager Payments
